249:  ['The younger witness','A younger neighbor asks what happened during the crisis. Adults disagree about how much truth is safe to share and whether the child should hear the hard parts.','How can a community tell the truth without handing its pain to children to carry?',[['Offer an honest account suited to the listener’s questions','Tell the truth with care for age and choice','honesty','You trusted a young person with truth while respecting their pace.'],['Invite the child to speak with several trusted adults','Make support wider than one storyteller','community','You made hard knowledge something no one had to hold alone.']]],
250:  ['A future not earned by suffering','A chance to leave the valley or pursue a long-held hope appears. Some survivors worry that choosing joy means abandoning the people who stayed.','Can a person honor the past without living inside its emergency forever?',[['Choose the future and make a mutual plan to remain connected','Let love survive a change of place','hope','You made growth compatible with loyalty.'],['Stay for now, but name what would make leaving possible later','Turn duty into a choice with a horizon','self-direction','You refused to let gratitude become a life sentence.']]]]),
251: buildExpandedStory('twilight','Twilight: The Choice Between Worlds','Stephenie Meyer’s novels','Love & belonging','🌙','love',[
252:  ['Bella Swan','A newcomer drawn toward a family unlike her own','Independent and curious, she wants to choose her life without confusing danger or intensity for proof of love.'],['Edward Cullen','A guarded young man afraid of the harm he could cause','Thoughtful but controlling when frightened, he must learn that protection without consent can become another form of danger.'],['Jacob Black','A friend connected to a close-knit community','Warm and proud, he is learning that loyalty does not entitle anyone to another person’s affection or future.']],
253:  ['Families, chosen kin, and the boundaries that protect them',['Three generations before the young newcomers meet, two communities build traditions for surviving secrecy, conflict, and change. Elders teach that keeping people safe requires honest boundaries, not only fierce loyalty.','Their children inherit stories of old bargains and old injuries. Some relatives mistake silence for peace; others insist that any promise made under pressure must be reconsidered.','One generation before Bella arrives, the families carry both an ability to protect one another and a danger: love can become a justification for deciding someone else’s life.']],
254:  [['The new town','A student arrives in a rainy town where classmates seem to know more about one another than they say. A magnetic stranger keeps distance, then returns with warnings but few explanations.','Can attraction grow safely when important facts are withheld?',[['Ask for honesty and take time before making a decision','Let curiosity keep its own pace','discernment','You made room for interest without surrendering the right to know.'],['Build friendships and routines outside the new relationship','Keep more than one source of belonging','independence','You protected a life broad enough to remain your own.']]],
255:  ['A warning framed as protection','Someone says that staying away is the only way to keep you safe, then tries to make that decision for you. The risk may be real, but so is your need for agency.','What makes protection different from control?',[['Ask for clear information and choose your own safety boundaries','Make consent part of care','boundaries','You treated safety as a shared plan, not an order.'],['Bring a trusted friend into the conversation','Avoid becoming isolated by someone else’s fear','support','You widened the circle before deciding what trust could hold.']]],
256:  ['The community’s old hurt','A family secret and an inherited feud shape how people read every gesture. Friends urge you to choose a side before you understand what each group fears.','Can you acknowledge history without accepting its rules?',[['Hear the people affected while refusing threats and coercion','Separate understanding from surrender','justice','You made room for history without letting it dictate your boundaries.'],['Step back until everyone can speak without a loyalty test','Refuse a choice made under pressure','prudence','You gave yourself time rather than making fear the judge.']]],
257:  ['A future by mutual choice','The danger eases, but a lasting relationship would require honesty, respect, and room for both people to change. No promise can guarantee that love removes risk.','What promise is worth carrying forward?',[['Choose a relationship only with clear boundaries and independent support','Let love strengthen autonomy','partnership','You made closeness answer to respect and an ongoing choice.'],['Choose distance while keeping compassion for everyone involved','Let care include a no','self-respect','You honored the possibility of love without owing it your future.']]]]),
258: buildExpandedStory('harry-potter','Harry Potter: What the Hallows Cannot Mend','J. K. Rowling’s novels','Belonging & courage','🪄','adventure',[
259:  ['Harry Potter','A young wizard carrying a history others interpret for him','Brave and loyal, he is tired of being treated as a symbol and must learn when to ask others to share the burden.'],['Hermione Granger','A student who turns knowledge into action','Brilliant and principled, she wants to help without carrying every plan alone or mistaking correctness for listening.'],['Neville Longbottom','A classmate growing beyond others’ expectations','Gentle and determined, he is discovering that courage can be quiet, collective, and still change a school.']],
260:  ['Wizards, Muggles, and the families excluded from official histories',['Three generations before the familiar students, families preserve magical and non-magical knowledge in kitchens, libraries, and workshops. Some hide their skills for safety; others argue that secrecy can leave unfair rules untouched.','Their children inherit stories of persecution and of institutions that promised protection while excluding certain families. A few keep testimony that challenges the heroic myths taught in public.','One generation before Harry’s arrival, the community carries love and resilience alongside unresolved prejudice, and a question about who gets to define what counts as belonging.']],
261:  [['A letter and a locked door','A young person learns that an entire world has existed just beyond the life adults allowed them to see. The invitation promises belonging, but also brings old expectations and new dangers.','How can a person enter a new world without letting it decide who they are?',[['Ask questions about the rules and who they protect','Make welcome compatible with scrutiny','curiosity','You treated belonging as an invitation to understand, not an order to conform.'],['Keep a connection to people and places outside the new institution','Carry more than one home with you','belonging','You made identity wider than any single house or label.']]],
262:  ['The rule that protects some','A school rule is presented as tradition, though its costs fall unevenly on students with less influence. Challenging it could risk a fragile sense of acceptance.','When does loyalty to a community mean changing it?',[['Gather accounts from those most affected before speaking publicly','Let evidence include lived experience','equity','You made the rule answer to the people living under it.'],['Find allies and ask for a safer way to challenge it','Share risk instead of demanding a lone hero','solidarity','You turned courage into a practice others could sustain.']]],
263:  ['A friend’s secret','A friend hides a painful truth because they fear losing trust. You feel hurt and want an immediate explanation, but the secret may involve shame or danger.','How can friendship ask for honesty without claiming ownership of another person’s story?',[['Explain the effect of the silence and ask what they can share safely','Pair candor with patience','honesty','You named your hurt without making disclosure a punishment.'],['Offer support and agree on a time to revisit the conversation','Keep the relationship open without forcing it','patience','You let trust have a future without demanding it all at once.']]],
264:  ['After the great battle','The immediate threat is over, but old institutions and prejudices remain. Students who survived disagree about whether returning to normal is possible or even desirable.','What should a victory change beyond the names in charge?',[['Give students and families real power to revise the rules','Make repair part of peace','reform','You treated survival as the start of rebuilding, not proof that all was well.'],['Honor losses and make long-term support part of the school’s duty','Let remembrance include care','healing','You refused to leave survivors alone with the cost of victory.']]]]),
265: buildExpandedStory('fifty-shades','Fifty Shades: Terms Freely Chosen','E. L. James’s novels','Trust & boundaries','🖋️','love',[
266:  ['Anastasia Steele','A young woman exploring intimacy and ambition','Thoughtful and curious, she wants desire to coexist with a clear voice, privacy, and the freedom to change her mind.'],['Christian Grey','A successful man whose past shapes his need for control','Charismatic and guarded, he must learn that generosity cannot replace consent and that vulnerability is not a contract.'],['Kate Kavanagh','A friend who asks direct questions','Loyal and outspoken, she wants to support without deciding another adult’s choices for them.']],
267:  ['Households learning how trust differs from control',['Three generations before the present-day couple, a family and its chosen kin inherit very different ideas about privacy, money, and who gets to set the terms of a relationship. Older relatives pass down both protective wisdom and silence around harm.','Their children build careers and partnerships while confronting the way status can make refusal feel costly. Friends create a habit of checking in privately, without turning concern into surveillance.','One generation before the story, the community carries a clear lesson: trust grows through freely chosen agreements, and every person retains the right to pause, renegotiate, or leave.']],
268:  [['An intense beginning','A meeting sparks attraction, but unequal wealth and experience complicate the attention. A confident offer arrives before the two people have learned how each handles disagreement.','What should come before a promise?',[['Talk through hopes, limits, and what each person can freely refuse','Put consent ahead of momentum','consent','You made a real yes possible by protecting the right to say no.'],['Take time apart and consult a trusted friend','Let reflection be part of desire','discernment','You kept attraction from setting the timetable for your judgment.']]],
269:  ['The agreement','A written arrangement is offered as proof that expectations are clear. Yet clarity on paper cannot make an unequal bargain fair or prevent someone from changing their mind.','What makes an agreement genuinely mutual?',[['Ask for independent advice and time to consider every term','Protect choice from pressure','independence','You treated a pause as a right, not an obstacle to romance.'],['Name non-negotiable boundaries and invite an honest response','Make disagreement possible before commitment','boundaries','You asked whether the relationship could hold a clear no.']]],
270:  ['A boundary is tested','A boundary is crossed, followed by an apology and a promise that it will not happen again. The person harmed is unsure whether trust can return.','What matters more than a persuasive apology?',[['Ask for changed behavior and outside support, not reassurance alone','Tie trust to accountable action','accountability','You made repair depend on what happens next, not on pressure to forgive.'],['Take distance while deciding what feels safe','Let uncertainty protect your choice','self-respect','You gave yourself room without owing anyone immediate reconciliation.']]],
271:  ['A future with room to change','The couple considers building a life together. Love is present, but so are differences in power, privacy, and the meaning of commitment.','What would make a shared future safe enough to choose?',[['Agree on ongoing check-ins, independent friendships, and the right to renegotiate','Make consent a continuing practice','partnership','You treated commitment as a series of freely renewed choices.'],['Choose separate paths and keep the lessons about boundaries','Let an ending be a complete answer','courage','You recognized that affection does not obligate a shared future.']]]]),
272: buildExpandedStory('crossfire','Crossfire: The Space Between Yes and No','Sylvia Day’s Crossfire novels','Trust & recovery','🌹','love',[
273:  ['Eva Tramell','A survivor rebuilding a life on her own terms','Driven and perceptive, she wants closeness without surrendering the hard-won boundaries that make her feel safe.'],['Gideon Cross','A powerful executive confronting old trauma','Controlled and protective, he must learn that secrecy and rescue can repeat harm even when motivated by fear.'],['Cary Taylor','A friend negotiating love, health, and belonging','Funny and candid, he wants care that does not make his complicated life a burden or a spectacle.']],
274:  ['Families and chosen kin learning to live beyond old wounds',['Three generations before the present-day friends, families pass down silence about violence, class, and the appearance of respectable households. A few relatives quietly make safe rooms where people can speak without being asked to prove their pain.','Their children learn to protect one another, sometimes by keeping secrets that later make trust difficult. A community advocate helps them see that support can be private, professional, and chosen.','One generation before Eva’s story, the inheritance is both tenderness and vigilance: love can help people heal, but it cannot replace autonomy, time, or skilled support.']],
275:  [['A familiar face in a new life','Two people meet while carrying histories they have not chosen to share. Attraction arrives alongside unease, and both are tempted to treat chemistry as certainty.','How can closeness begin without requiring disclosure?',[['Share only what feels safe and ask for the same in return','Let trust build at a chosen pace','boundaries','You made privacy compatible with connection.'],['Talk about what behavior would help each person feel respected','Make care concrete before it becomes a promise','respect','You asked for a relationship that could be experienced, not merely declared.']]],
276:  ['The past returns','A trigger or painful memory unsettles one partner. The other wants to fix it immediately, but the person affected has not asked to be rescued.','What does support look like when you cannot take the pain away?',[['Ask whether they want listening, practical help, or space','Offer options without taking over','attunement','You let the person affected define what help could mean.'],['Suggest professional support and offer to help find choices','Respect the limits of what a partner can provide','care','You made room for expertise without treating it as a cure on command.']]],
277:  ['A choice under pressure','An important decision is tangled with money, family expectations, and fear of abandonment. Neither person wants to lose the relationship, but agreement obtained through fear would not be trust.','Can love remain when one person says not yet?',[['Pause the decision and make sure both can choose independently','Protect a yes from the fear of loss','prudence','You refused to treat urgency as proof of devotion.'],['State your own boundary and accept that the answer may differ','Make honesty safer than appeasement','integrity','You allowed a difficult truth to matter more than keeping the peace.']]],
278:  ['The work of staying—or leaving','The couple faces the slow work of repairing patterns. Friends remind them that healing is not a promise to remain together at any cost.','What does a healthy next chapter require?',[['Choose ongoing support, accountability, and mutual freedom','Let hope be supported by practice','healing','You made change a shared effort that neither person had to supervise alone.'],['Step away with care and keep the support network intact','Let safety be a valid ending','self-respect','You chose a future not defined by whether the relationship continued.']]]]),
279: buildExpandedStory('thomas-covenant','The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant: The Measure of Belief','Stephen R. Donaldson’s novels','Belief & accountability','🪨','ideas',[
280:  ['Thomas Covenant','A wounded outsider whose choices affect a world he doubts','Defensive and ashamed, he fears that belief will make him responsible for every consequence—and that disbelief can excuse harm.'],['Linden Avery','A physician learning where care meets uncertainty','Perceptive and determined, she must distinguish compassion from taking control of another person’s healing.'],['A Land-bearer','A community member living with the cost of grand quests','Resilient and skeptical of saviors, insisting that people in danger are more than tests for a hero.']],
281:  ['Healers, land-keepers, and the stories people trust',['Three generations before the strangers arrive, a community of healers and growers keeps records of illness, harvest, and the promises made by those seeking help. Their teachings value care but disagree about whether hope can survive repeated failure.','Their children inherit stories of a land that answers attention, along with warnings against leaders who claim suffering proves a person’s worth. Some preserve practical medicine; others keep the names of people harmed by noble causes.','One generation before the familiar crisis, the community carries a fragile faith in renewal and a clear demand: anyone who acts in another’s name must answer to them.']],
282:  [['A world that might be real','A stranger wakes in a place that seems impossible. The people around him need help, but he fears that taking their claims seriously will make him responsible for events he cannot understand.','What does uncertainty permit—and what does it not excuse?',[['Ask what the people need now, without pretending to know the whole world','Let care precede certainty','humility','You treated uncertainty as a reason to listen, not to dismiss suffering.'],['Tell the truth about your doubts and stay to witness the consequences','Make honesty answerable to action','accountability','You refused both false certainty and convenient distance.']]],
283:  ['The power offered','A rare gift could stop an immediate threat, but using it without the community’s knowledge might damage the land or expose its people to retaliation.','Who should shape a decision whose cost others will bear?',[['Explain the risk and ask the affected community to decide with you','Share authority before using power','equity','You made the people at risk participants, not scenery.'],['Decline until safeguards and a second opinion are available','Treat restraint as a responsible choice','prudence','You let urgency meet a boundary before it became harm.']]],
284:  ['A wound that cannot be undone','A choice made in fear has injured trust. A public apology is possible, but the harmed person does not owe forgiveness or a quick return to the group.','What can accountability offer when it cannot erase the past?',[['Name the harm and ask what repair is wanted','Put the harmed person’s needs before absolution','repair','You made responsibility a practice rather than a plea for comfort.'],['Accept distance and support the community’s safety plan','Respect a boundary even when it hurts','respect','You did not make forgiveness the price of taking responsibility.']]],
285:  ['The work of renewal','The immediate danger recedes. People disagree about whether to rebuild the old order, leave, or create something new with safeguards against repeating its failures.','What should hope ask of those who inherit the aftermath?',[['Support a shared council with power to revise its decisions','Build a future that can correct itself','community','You made renewal collective and open to challenge.'],['Stay as a learner and take on unglamorous work','Let service follow rather than lead','service','You chose a place in the work without claiming its story as yours.']]]]),
286: buildExpandedStory('indiana-jones','Indiana Jones: The Map of Many Hands','Harrison Ford’s Indiana Jones films','Discovery & stewardship','🧭','adventure',[
287:  ['Indiana Jones','An archaeologist drawn toward a contested discovery','Witty and daring, he must decide whether curiosity grants ownership or creates a duty to listen.'],['Sallah','A trusted colleague with deep local knowledge','Warm and capable, he refuses to be treated as a helper in someone else’s legend.'],['Marion Ravenwood','An independent partner with her own stake in the past','Candid and resourceful, she expects respect, shared credit, and a say in the risks.']],
288:  ['Families of craftspeople, guides, and keepers of local memory',['Three generations before the expedition, families preserve maps, craft, and oral histories through changing borders and outside claims of ownership. Their records carry practical knowledge alongside the names of people whose contributions were erased.','Their children teach visitors how to ask permission and how to leave sacred places undisturbed. Some are pressured to trade knowledge for safety or money; others create agreements that give communities a real veto.','One generation before the familiar archaeologist arrives, guides and keepers inherit both curiosity and a rule: discovery is not a license to take, and credit belongs with the people who kept knowledge alive.']],
289:  [['The sealed chamber','An expedition finds an artifact in a place that local residents consider part of their living history. A museum sponsor wants it removed before anyone can object.','Who has the right to decide what discovery means?',[['Pause the excavation and ask local keepers what they want','Make consent part of scholarship','respect','You put stewardship ahead of a dramatic find.'],['Document the site together before any decision is made','Share knowledge and credit','equity','You made the record belong to more than the expedition.']]],
290:  ['A guide’s warning','A colleague explains that the proposed route risks damaging a place still used by the community. The sponsor calls the concern superstition.','How should expertise be recognized?',[['Change the plan and credit the people who raised the concern','Let local knowledge shape the work','humility','You treated experience as evidence, not an obstacle.'],['Invite an independent community review before continuing','Build accountability into the expedition','discernment','You made the decision answerable to people who bear its consequences.']]],
291:  ['What the museum receives','The expedition can claim a headline-making victory, or support a community-led return and preservation plan that may keep the artifact out of public view.','What should a successful expedition leave behind?',[['Fund preservation under local authority and share the full record','Make stewardship last beyond the discovery','responsibility','You helped return control along with the story.'],['Accept that some knowledge is not yours to publish','Let restraint be part of respect','restraint','You chose not to turn access into entitlement.']]]]),
292: buildExpandedStory('star-wars','Star Wars: A New Hope for the Next Generation','Harrison Ford and Mark Hamill’s Star Wars characters','Belonging & rebellion','✨','adventure',[
293:  ['Luke Skywalker','A young pilot longing for a life beyond inherited limits','Hopeful and impulsive, learning that courage means choosing with others rather than chasing a destiny alone.'],['Han Solo','A smuggler whose self-reliance hides a capacity for loyalty','Clever and guarded, he wants freedom but must decide what responsibility he owes to people in danger.'],['Leia Organa','A leader carrying both public duty and private grief','Strategic and uncompromising, she insists that resistance must make room for the people it claims to protect.']],
294:  ['Households, pilots, and communities living under distant rule',['Three generations before the rebellion, farming families, mechanics, and travelers keep local knowledge alive under taxes and changing authorities. They remember both the courage that protected neighbors and the compromises that left some people unprotected.','Their children inherit hidden routes and stories of resistance, but also fear that one dramatic hero will eclipse the ordinary people who sustain change. A network of mutual aid begins recording every contributor.','One generation before the young rebels meet, communities pass forward a mixed legacy of daring, grief, and practical solidarity—and ask whether liberation can change who gets to make decisions.']],
295:  [['A call from far away','A message reveals that people on another world need help. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the choice adventure in `index.html` with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories where inherited struggles and player choices shape characters and endings.
- Integrate the requested actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings into the adventure library and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should meaningfully affect character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- The hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; a `books` array and `buildExpandedStory` definitions are present.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

## Objective
- Expand the choice adventure in `index.html` with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories where inherited struggles and player choices shape characters and endings.
- Integrate actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings into the adventure library and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should meaningfully affect character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` to identify requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- The hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; a `books` array and `buildExpandedStory` definitions are present.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories and integrate actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings into the library and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active

153: gatsby:['A circle of workers, renters, and neighbors around the bay',['Before the bright parties, a shoreline household keeps a ledger of wages, borrowed rooms, and promises made by people with very different amounts of money.','Their children move between service, city work, and new fortunes. 154: flies:['A school community and the households that send children into its care',['Long before the island, families and caretakers pass down practical knowledge: how to share food, settle a quarrel, and notice who has been left out.','A later generation grows up amid adult rules that reward obedience more readily than listening. 155: 'animal-farm':['A community of farm animals across changing owners and seasons',['Before the rebellion is imaginable, older animals teach where food is stored, which fences fail, and how work is divided. 156: 'swiss-family':['A family tradition of making do, learning, and mutual care',['Several generations before the familiar household, relatives and neighbors preserve maps, recipes, repairs, and stories of journeys that went wrong as well as right.','A later generation turns those lessons into habits: divide the work, ask what everyone needs, and treat a new place as something to understand rather than own.','By the time the familiar family’s children arrive, they inherit curiosity and resourcefulness—but also the responsibility to decide what kind of home their skills will build.']],
157: 'treasure-island':['A port-side network of sailors, innkeepers, and shore families',['Long before the map appears, a harbor household learns that useful knowledge travels by word of mouth: which captains pay fairly, which promises need checking, and who can be trusted in a storm.','Their children enter a port where adventure and exploitation share the same bright language. 158: 'west-side':['Two neighborhood networks shaped by migration, work, and changing borders',['Before the young dancers are born, families and chosen kin build lives in a city that keeps changing its rents, languages, and boundaries. 159: romeo:['Two households and the wider community around an old feud',['Generations before the young lovers, a dispute over status and influence begins to harden into a family story. 160: 'charlottes-web':['A farm community of animals, caretakers, and small acts of attention',['Long before the familiar barn friends, generations pass along quiet knowledge of seasons, shelter, and which lives are treated as useful only when they serve someone else.','A later generation makes a practice of noticing the small and overlooked: a safe corner, a shared warning, a life worth protecting beyond its market value.','The youngest have not yet arrived, but the barn already holds an inheritance of companionship—and the question of whether care can change the rules around it.']],

162: oliver:['A city neighborhood of working families and mutual-aid households',['Long before the familiar child is born, city families make networks of care amid scarce wages, crowded rooms, and institutions that treat poverty as a personal fault.','A later generation shares meals, work, warnings, and temporary shelter. 171: northwest:['A family of clerks, station workers, and people whose names are often overlooked',['Long before the mistaken identity, generations of ordinary workers learn how a missing record or an assumed name can alter a person’s safety. 172: 'maltese-falcon':['A neighborhood circle of office workers, porters, and independent tradespeople',['Before the famous object changes hands, generations of workers around the city learn to read contracts, clients, and the difference between a polished story and a reliable one.','A later generation keeps shared records and practical alliances, especially for those whose expertise is ignored until it becomes useful to someone powerful.','The familiar investigators are not yet born. 173: 'death-on-nile':['A river community of boat workers, guides, families, and travelers',['Generations before the luxury steamer, river families sustain livelihoods through navigation, seasonal knowledge, and skilled work that wealthy visitors often mistake for scenery.','A later generation watches fortunes travel through the region while local labor remains undervalued. ## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories and integrate actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings into the library and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` to identify requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; a `books` array and `buildExpandedStory` definitions are present.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories and actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` to identify requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; a `books` array and `buildExpandedStory` definitions are present.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational stories and actor-inspired characters and book/series reimaginings.

## Requirements
- Include characters and roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related books and series.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; choices and feelings should shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.

## Decisions
- Stories are original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; a `books` array and `buildExpandedStory` definitions are present.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational reimaginings inspired by requested actors, films, books, and series.

## Requirements
- Include roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related works.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; let choices and feelings shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.
- Create original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.

## Decisions
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate syntax, story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; the page displays “22 illustrated adventures.”
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational reimaginings inspired by requested actors, films, books, and series.

## Requirements
- Include roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related works.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; let choices and feelings shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.
- Create original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.

## Decisions
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.
- Verified JavaScript embedded in `index.html` parses successfully with Node.

### Active
- Integrate and complete requested book and series stories in the adventure library and gameplay.
- Expand actor-role coverage to include all requested figures.
- Validate story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; the page displays “22 illustrated adventures.”
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational reimaginings inspired by requested actors, films, books, and series.
- Integrate the stories into the adventure library and gameplay, then validate the experience.

## Requirements
- Include roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related works.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; let choices and feelings shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.
- Create original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.

## Decisions
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.
- Verified embedded JavaScript in `index.html` parses successfully with Node.

### Active
- Inspect which expanded stories are integrated into the adventure library and gameplay.
- Complete requested book and series story coverage and actor-role coverage.
- Validate story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; the page displays “22 illustrated adventures.”
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand `index.html`’s choice adventure with emotionally consequential, multigenerational reimaginings inspired by the requested actors, films, books, and series.
- Integrate the stories into the adventure library and gameplay, then validate the experience.

## Requirements
- Include roles associated with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jeff Speakman, Bruce Lee, Robin Williams, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Harrison Ford, and Mark Hamill.
- Include *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, *Crossfire*, and related works.
- Explore parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents; let choices and feelings shape character development and endings.
- Show light and dark sides, including less prominent characters.
- Create original reimaginings, not claims about source canon.

## Decisions
- Where literal ancestry does not fit, use family, chosen kin, household, community, or inherited tradition.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added actor-inspired adventures for *Rocky*, *First Blood*, *The Terminator*, *Predator*, *Conan*, *Bloodsport*, *The Perfect Weapon*, *Mad Max*, *Gladiator*, *Good Will Hunting*, and *Enter the Dragon*.
- Added story material for *The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant*, *Indiana Jones*, and *Star Wars*.
- Added `buildExpandedStory` definitions for *The Neverending Story*, *The Tomorrow Series*, *The Ellie Chronicles*, *Twilight*, *Harry Potter*, *Fifty Shades*, and *Crossfire*.
- Verified embedded JavaScript in `index.html` parses successfully with Node.

### Active
- Inspect which expanded stories are integrated into the adventure library and gameplay.
- Complete requested book and series story coverage and actor-role coverage.
- Validate story structure, playthrough outcomes, and displayed adventure count.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for requested stories and definitions that exist but are not integrated.
2. Complete and integrate missing stories, casts, histories, and gameplay behavior.
3. Validate the experience and update the displayed count if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story library, interface, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Hero text says “22 original reimaginings”; the page displays “22 illustrated adventures.”
- Recent inspection found story definitions near lines 176–179 and 272; whether expanded stories are integrated remains unresolved.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `data.tmp`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.

141: 'charlie-wonka':[['Charlie','A thoughtful child invited into a strange factory','Grateful for possibility without wanting wonder to cost someone else their dignity.'],['Violet','A competitive visitor','Confident and ambitious, learning when determination stops being fun and starts ignoring warnings.'],['Grandpa Joe','A family storyteller and companion','Joyful about a second chance, conscious that a child should not have to carry every adult hope.']],
142: wonka:[['Willy Wonka','A young inventor with a big dream','Energized by possibility, learning that a brilliant idea is only as good as the way it treats its collaborators.'],['Noodle','A sharp, resourceful new friend','Suspicious of easy promises, brave enough to hope when someone gives her a real choice.'],['Abacus','A careful planner in the group','Anxious about risk but proud of the skills that turn a dream into a workable plan.']],
143: 'gone-with-wind':[['Mammy','A skilled woman whose labor has been taken for granted','Protective and clear-eyed, with her own judgment, boundaries, and hopes beyond managing other people.'],['Melanie Hamilton','A neighbor choosing care amid upheaval','Gentle without being blind, determined to help people without pretending the old order was just.'],['A newly freed neighbor','A person building a future after enslavement','Carrying hard-won hope and insisting that safety, wages, land, and choice belong in the future.']],
144: casablanca:[['Ilsa Lund','A traveler facing an impossible choice','Affectionate and conflicted, wanting her future to be hers rather than a prize in someone else’s sacrifice.'],['Sam','A pianist and trusted friend','Loyal, observant, and tired of being treated as background when he understands the room better than anyone.'],['Captain Renault','An official deciding what his authority is for','Cynical in public, increasingly aware that neutrality can protect the powerful.']],
145: northwest:[['Eve Kendall','An operative living inside a dangerous cover','Composed by necessity, lonely under the performance, and weighing when trust becomes possible.'],['Roger Thornhill','A stranger mistaken for someone else','Witty and unsettled, trying to regain control without letting fear make every decision.'],['Philip Vandamm','A confident strategist used to directing others','Patient and calculating, with a choice between treating people as pieces or facing their agency.']],
146: 'maltese-falcon':[['Effie Perine','A private investigator’s capable secretary','Sharp, self-possessed, and tired of being the person everyone overlooks until they need her evidence.'],['Brigid O’Shaughnessy','A client with a carefully managed story','Afraid of losing control, capable of both tenderness and manipulation, and responsible for the choices she makes.'],['Joel Cairo','A precise collector with his own stake','Proud and guarded, wanting to be taken seriously beyond the assumptions others make about him.']],
147: 'death-on-nile':[['Salome Otterbourne','A writer among wealthy travelers','Observant and outspoken, alert to the stories powerful guests would rather keep private.'],['Jacqueline de Bellefort','A passenger carrying heartbreak','Hurt and intensely focused, facing the difference between feeling wronged and choosing what to do next.'],['Colonel Race','An investigator aboard the ship','Methodical and humane, aware that a confident theory can ruin an innocent life.']],
148: 'orient-express':[['Mary Debenham','A passenger with a guarded past','Self-controlled and watchful, wanting privacy while understanding that silence shapes the fate of others.'],['Dr. Arbuthnot','A physician and skeptical witness','Protective and principled, questioning whether official rules always deliver a just result.'],['Monsieur Bouc','A railway director with influence','Sociable but under pressure, discovering that fairness is more than keeping order.']]

153: gatsby:['A circle of workers, renters, and neighbors around the bay',['Before the bright parties, a shoreline household keeps a ledger of wages, borrowed rooms, and promises made by people with very different amounts of money.','Their children move between service, city work, and new fortunes. A neighbor’s account of who paid for each polished room becomes an inheritance of its own.','One generation later, the young learn that a name can open doors—and hide the labor behind them. They are not yet the people of the familiar story, but the bay’s old inequalities are already shaping its choices.']],
154: flies:['A school community and the households that send children into its care',['Long before the island, families and caretakers pass down practical knowledge: how to share food, settle a quarrel, and notice who has been left out.','A later generation grows up amid adult rules that reward obedience more readily than listening. Some keep the old lessons alive in kitchens, classrooms, and games.','By the time the children of the familiar story are born, they inherit both the possibility of cooperation and habits of hierarchy they did not choose.']],
155: 'animal-farm':['A community of farm animals across changing owners and seasons',['Before the rebellion is imaginable, older animals teach where food is stored, which fences fail, and how work is divided. Their memory is practical—and easy for a new authority to dismiss.','Their young see rules change with each season. Some begin repeating the old warnings; others learn that a written promise means little if only a few can read it.','The generation before the familiar farm story inherits a dream of fairness alongside the hard lesson that power can rewrite memory.']],
156: 'swiss-family':['A family tradition of making do, learning, and mutual care',['Several generations before the familiar household, relatives and neighbors preserve maps, recipes, repairs, and stories of journeys that went wrong as well as right.','A later generation turns those lessons into habits: divide the work, ask what everyone needs, and treat a new place as something to understand rather than own.','By the time the familiar family’s children arrive, they inherit curiosity and resourcefulness—but also the responsibility to decide what kind of home their skills will build.']],
157: 'treasure-island':['A port-side network of sailors, innkeepers, and shore families',['Long before the map appears, a harbor household learns that useful knowledge travels by word of mouth: which captains pay fairly, which promises need checking, and who can be trusted in a storm.','Their children enter a port where adventure and exploitation share the same bright language. A few keep careful records; others make alliances so no one must rely on a stranger’s charm alone.','The next generation grows up hearing sea stories—and warnings that treasure is never worth more than the people asked to risk their lives for it.']],
158: 'west-side':['Two neighborhood networks shaped by migration, work, and changing borders',['Before the young dancers are born, families and chosen kin build lives in a city that keeps changing its rents, languages, and boundaries. Elders remember how often outsiders benefit when working people are set against one another.','The young inherit both a rich sense of belonging and a feud already older than they are. Whether that history becomes a wall or a warning is not settled yet.']],
159: romeo:['Two households and the wider community around an old feud',['Generations before the young lovers, a dispute over status and influence begins to harden into a family story. The first witnesses remember practical grievances, not an eternal hatred.','Children inherit the feud as a rule of belonging. Some relatives quietly keep friendships across it; others fear that questioning the story will endanger the household.','By the time the familiar young people are born, the quarrel has become an inheritance no child agreed to receive—and no child should have to resolve alone.']],
160: 'charlottes-web':['A farm community of animals, caretakers, and small acts of attention',['Long before the familiar barn friends, generations pass along quiet knowledge of seasons, shelter, and which lives are treated as useful only when they serve someone else.','A later generation makes a practice of noticing the small and overlooked: a safe corner, a shared warning, a life worth protecting beyond its market value.','The youngest have not yet arrived, but the barn already holds an inheritance of companionship—and the question of whether care can change the rules around it.']],
161: huck:['A river community of families, workers, and people seeking freedom',['Before the familiar raft journey, generations along the river share routes, food, and news. Some are denied freedom by law; their knowledge and choices persist despite systems built to control them.','A later generation witnesses laws and customs presented as unquestionable. Within families and chosen networks, people teach each other to read danger, seek allies, and name injustice plainly.','The children of the familiar story are not yet born. They will inherit both the river’s routes to possibility and a society whose cruelties demand more than private kindness.']],
162: oliver:['A city neighborhood of working families and mutual-aid households',['Long before the familiar child is born, city families make networks of care amid scarce wages, crowded rooms, and institutions that treat poverty as a personal fault.','A later generation shares meals, work, warnings, and temporary shelter. They know that one act of rescue matters, but cannot by itself repair the conditions that make rescue necessary.','The next child inherits a city of sharp risks and generous people—and a question the adults have not answered: who will make safety something everyone can count on?']],
163: 'king-and-i':['A household of teachers, court workers, and local scholars',['Before the familiar court and classroom meet, generations preserve knowledge through family teaching, local scholarship, and careful negotiation with distant powers.','A later generation sees outsiders mistake unfamiliar customs for ignorance. Relatives and mentors teach children to ask who is speaking, who is being translated, and who holds authority.','The young of the familiar story have not yet been born, but they will enter a world already shaped by unequal power and by people who have long been thinking for themselves.']],
164: 'sound-music':['A household of musicians, caregivers, and neighbors in a changing Europe',['Generations before the familiar family, songs, work, and shared rituals help relatives stay connected through political change. They pass down not only melodies but practical ways to care for one another.','A later generation watches public life grow more coercive. Some learn that keeping a household safe requires quiet planning, trusted allies, and room for every member to speak.','The children of the familiar story are still in the future. Their inheritance is music and affection, but also the knowledge that joy needs courage and a plan when power turns threatening.']],
165: alice:['A family of storytellers, puzzle-makers, and curious children',['Long before the familiar child follows a hurried rabbit, relatives and chosen kin trade puzzles and stories that let children question rules without being punished for wondering.','A later generation grows up among adults who sometimes confuse good manners with unquestioning obedience. A few keep wonder alive as a way to notice when a rule makes no sense.','The next child is not yet born. They will inherit a world of strange instructions—and the permission, if someone passes it on, to ask who made them.']],
166: 'mary-poppins':['A city household and its circle of caregivers across generations',['Before the familiar family, generations of city caregivers learn how to make time for children in streets and homes organized around adult work. Songs and games carry attention across busy days.','A later generation inherits schedules that leave little room for listening. Neighbors and relatives quietly preserve rituals of play, noticing that children’s worries do not disappear just because adults are occupied.','The familiar children are not yet born, but they will inherit both the pressure of a hurried household and a tradition of making wonder—and attention—part of ordinary life.']],
167: 'charlie-wonka':['A working family and the neighborhood that shares its table',['Long before the golden ticket, a family and its neighbors stretch small resources through shared meals, practical skills, and stories that make scarcity less lonely.','A later generation sees wealth celebrated as spectacle while the people doing essential work remain out of sight. They pass on the belief that delight means more when it is shared fairly.','The child of the familiar story is still years away. Their inheritance includes hope, humor, and a clear-eyed question about who gets to enjoy a wonder built by many hands.']],
168: wonka:['A line of makers, market sellers, and chosen collaborators',['Generations before the young inventor arrives, makers trade recipes and craft knowledge while learning how guilds and gatekeepers can restrict who gets to sell their work.','A later generation experiments together, sharing credit and warning one another about bargains that turn friendship into unpaid labor. Their small collaborations keep a different kind of business imaginable.','The young dreamer has not yet been born. They will inherit both ambition and a community lesson: invention is not a triumph if its costs are pushed onto unseen helpers.']],
169: 'gone-with-wind':['Black families and a wider community navigating enslavement, emancipation, and its aftermath',['Generations before the familiar characters, enslaved Black families build kinship, knowledge, and care under a violent system that denies their freedom and often tears families apart. Their lives and choices are not a backdrop to someone else’s story.','After emancipation, a later generation pursues family reunification, safety, education, fair wages, and land amid organized efforts to restrict those freedoms. Community networks carry skills and memory where institutions fail them.','The familiar cast is not yet born. The world they will enter is already shaped by slavery’s violence and by Black people’s agency, resistance, and ongoing struggle for material freedom.']],
170: casablanca:['A North African neighborhood network of families, port workers, and newcomers',['Before the familiar café, generations in a port community build ties across languages and arrivals. They keep routes, contacts, and food moving when official borders make ordinary life precarious.','A later generation faces shifting authorities and new waves of people seeking safety. Neighbors debate how to help without turning refuge into a favor owed.','The familiar travelers are still in the future. They will inherit a city whose hospitality and compromises were shaped by generations of people making room under pressure.']],
171: northwest:['A family of clerks, station workers, and people whose names are often overlooked',['Long before the mistaken identity, generations of ordinary workers learn how a missing record or an assumed name can alter a person’s safety. They preserve details others consider too small to matter.','A later generation works among institutions that prize confident explanations. Their household teaches caution: verify a claim, keep your own account, and do not confuse authority with truth.','The familiar strangers are not yet born. They will enter a world where people can be mistaken for pieces in someone else’s plan—and where careful witnesses can change what happens.']],
172: 'maltese-falcon':['A neighborhood circle of office workers, porters, and independent tradespeople',['Before the famous object changes hands, generations of workers around the city learn to read contracts, clients, and the difference between a polished story and a reliable one.','A later generation keeps shared records and practical alliances, especially for those whose expertise is ignored until it becomes useful to someone powerful.','The familiar investigators are not yet born. They will inherit a city where trust is negotiated, evidence can be buried, and overlooked people may see the decisive detail first.']],
173: 'death-on-nile':['A river community of boat workers, guides, families, and travelers',['Generations before the luxury steamer, river families sustain livelihoods through navigation, seasonal knowledge, and skilled work that wealthy visitors often mistake for scenery.','A later generation watches fortunes travel through the region while local labor remains undervalued. They teach their children to keep accounts, tell their own stories, and notice who benefits from a grand journey.','The familiar passengers are not yet born. Their mystery will unfold on a river already carrying many lives and histories beyond the guests’ view.']],
174: 'orient-express':['A railway community of workers, travelers, and families along the route',['Before the snowbound train, generations of railway workers and their families build lives around timetables, repair skills, and routes linking distant communities. Their labor makes other people’s journeys possible.','A later generation sees borders and official rules determine whose movement is easy and whose is questioned. Workers quietly share information and help one another stay safe across stations.','The familiar passengers have not yet been born. They will inherit a network held together by unseen labor—and a question about whose account counts when authority arrives.']]

191: ['The final exchange','The last match is close. 194: ['A family of teachers, shopkeepers, and neighbors',['Three generations before the return, relatives and neighbors share a small training hall, teaching self-defense alongside the responsibility to de-escalate.','Their children see the neighborhood change and learn that respectability can become an excuse to ignore people facing danger. 197: ['The old lesson','Your teacher offers a traditional response, but the person being targeted fears that a confrontation will make matters worse.','Can a useful tradition change when its old answer creates new danger?',[['Adapt the training into a shared safety plan','Use skill to widen everyone’s choices','resourcefulness','You treated tradition as living knowledge, not an order.'],['Invite a trusted mediator and document the pressure','Bring witnesses into a private struggle','transparency','You made it harder for anyone to deny what happened.']]],
198: ['A final test','The people causing harm offer a private bargain: one person’s silence in exchange for temporary peace.','What kind of peace can the neighborhood live with?',[['Reject the bargain and support a collective response','Share the risk rather than burden one person','solidarity','You chose a slower path with more people able to sustain it.'],['Accept a short pause while arranging outside help','Protect immediate safety without calling it a solution','prudence','You bought time, while keeping the unfinished problem in view.']]]]),

204: ['The convoy','Families flee along a route controlled by armed escorts. 213: buildFilmStory('good-will-hunting','Good Will Hunting: The Work of Staying','Robin Williams','Friendship & healing','📚','care',[
214: ['Sean Maguire','A counselor carrying grief and hard-earned patience','Warm but blunt, he must offer care without asking anyone to heal on his schedule.'],['Will Hunting','A brilliant young man wary of being known','Funny and defensive, afraid that accepting help will surrender control.'],['Skylar','A student building a future away from home','Affectionate and independent, unwilling to become someone else’s rescue plan.']],

216: [

218: ['An invitation west','A friend invites Will into a new life elsewhere. 230: buildExpandedStory('neverending','The Neverending Story: The Name You Choose','Michael Ende’s novel and its imagined worlds','Imagination & identity','🐉','adventure',[
231:  ['Bastian Balthazar Bux','A reader asked to enter a world in peril','Lonely and imaginative, longing to be seen; he must learn that a wish can create responsibility as well as escape.'],['Atreyu','A young quester carrying a people’s hope','Brave but still a child, he wants help without being mistaken for a symbol who cannot falter.'],['The Childlike Empress','A sovereign whose survival depends on renewal','Calm and curious, she knows restoration cannot mean returning to a world that excluded its most vulnerable.']],
232:  ['Readers, storytellers, and the worlds they pass between',['Three generations before the great book is opened, a family of printers and storytellers keeps a public reading room alive through hard seasons. 233:  [['The book with no ending','A forgotten book seems to answer a reader who feels invisible. 234:  ['A name spoken aloud','The quester reaches a border where every traveler is expected to surrender a name and a memory. 235:  ['A wish with consequences','A wish gives the hero influence over the story, but each change rearranges someone else’s life. 236:  ['The story carried home','The fading world begins to recover, but its future cannot depend on one brave visitor. 238:  ['Ellie Linton','A young person recording a community under occupation','Practical and observant, she wants to protect friends without mistaking fear-driven certainty for leadership.'],['Homer Yannos','A friend whose confidence can galvanize or overwhelm','Inventive and funny, he is learning that bold plans need consent from the people who bear their risks.'],['Lee Takkam','A thoughtful friend balancing love and responsibility','Quietly brave, wary of being reduced to a role in somebody else’s war story.']],
239:  ['A valley community and the memory of earlier upheavals',['Three generations before the young friends disappear into the hills, farm families and town workers share water, tools, and news. 240:  [['The valley goes quiet','Returning from a camping trip, a group of friends finds homes empty and familiar routines broken. 241:  ['The argument at the hideout','The group debates a risky act of resistance. 242:  ['A neighbor asks for help','A family outside the group needs medicine and a safe route. 243:  ['The record after danger','The occupation’s immediate threat shifts, but the valley is divided over what to remember. 244: buildExpandedStory('ellie-chronicles','The Ellie Chronicles: A Life After Survival','John Marsden’s Ellie Chronicles','Recovery & responsibility','🌱','care',[
245:  ['Ellie Linton','A survivor trying to build a life beyond emergency','Capable and vigilant, she struggles to believe ordinary hopes are not a betrayal of those lost.'],['A trusted friend','A fellow survivor choosing what comes next','Loyal but exhausted, needing a future not defined only by usefulness to others.'],['A younger neighbor','A young person growing up in the aftermath','Curious and watchful, carrying questions adults avoid because they fear reopening pain.']],
246:  ['Families and chosen kin learning what follows a crisis',['Three generations before the familiar survivors, rural households endure drought, displacement, and a long rebuilding. 247:  [['The quiet after the alarm','A new danger has passed, but ordinary sounds still startle the survivor. 248:  ['A friend pulls away','Someone close stops answering messages. 249:  ['The younger witness','A younger neighbor asks what happened during the crisis. 250:  ['A future not earned by suffering','A chance to leave the valley or pursue a long-held hope appears. 251: buildExpandedStory('twilight','Twilight: The Choice Between Worlds','Stephenie Meyer’s novels','Love & belonging','🌙','love',[
252:  ['Bella Swan','A newcomer drawn toward a family unlike her own','Independent and curious, she wants to choose her life without confusing danger or intensity for proof of love.'],['Edward Cullen','A guarded young man afraid of the harm he could cause','Thoughtful but controlling when frightened, he must learn that protection without consent can become another form of danger.'],['Jacob Black','A friend connected to a close-knit community','Warm and proud, he is learning that loyalty does not entitle anyone to another person’s affection or future.']],
253:  ['Families, chosen kin, and the boundaries that protect them',['Three generations before the young newcomers meet, two communities build traditions for surviving secrecy, conflict, and change. 254:  [['The new town','A student arrives in a rainy town where classmates seem to know more about one another than they say. 255:  ['A warning framed as protection','Someone says that staying away is the only way to keep you safe, then tries to make that decision for you. 256:  ['The community’s old hurt','A family secret and an inherited feud shape how people read every gesture. 257:  ['A future by mutual choice','The danger eases, but a lasting relationship would require honesty, respect, and room for both people to change. 258: buildExpandedStory('harry-potter','Harry Potter: What the Hallows Cannot Mend','J. K. Rowling’s novels','Belonging & courage','🪄','adventure',[
259:  ['Harry Potter','A young wizard carrying a history others interpret for him','Brave and loyal, he is tired of being treated as a symbol and must learn when to ask others to share the burden.'],['Hermione Granger','A student who turns knowledge into action','Brilliant and principled, she wants to help without carrying every plan alone or mistaking correctness for listening.'],['Neville Longbottom','A classmate growing beyond others’ expectations','Gentle and determined, he is discovering that courage can be quiet, collective, and still change a school.']],
260:  ['Wizards, Muggles, and the families excluded from official histories',['Three generations before the familiar students, families preserve magical and non-magical knowledge in kitchens, libraries, and workshops. 261:  [['A letter and a locked door','A young person learns that an entire world has existed just beyond the life adults allowed them to see. 262:  ['The rule that protects some','A school rule is presented as tradition, though its costs fall unevenly on students with less influence. 265: buildExpandedStory('fifty-shades','Fifty Shades: Terms Freely Chosen','E. L. James’s novels','Trust & boundaries','🖋️','love',[
